direction.name: Photographs at uneven sizes
direction.idea: A calm page where the pictures are placed like prints on a gallery wall: each at its own size and position, with text set small and light between them. Nothing lines up in the obvious way, yet everything sits on a grid you can feel. The unevenness is what makes it read as art-directed by a person: a small portrait far left, a wide landscape running off the right edge, a square that overlaps the next section. It lets photographs lead without ever becoming a slideshow.
direction.composition: A 12-column grid with wide margins (5–7vw). The hero is a single line of large light type (6–9vw) across the top third, and below it one photograph placed off-centre (columns 6–12, 16:10), its top edge overlapping the baseline zone of the headline by a few pixels of deliberate tension. Each following section places two or three photographs with different spans and vertical offsets: for example a 3:4 portrait in columns 2–5 starting 120px lower than a 16:10 landscape in columns 7–12; then a single small 1:1 in columns 9–11 beside a paragraph in columns 2–6. Paragraphs are short (max 40ch) and sit in the gaps. No two consecutive sections use the same arrangement. Vertical spacing is large and irregular on purpose (120–260px).
direction.typography: A light or regular weight at large size for the few headings; small, quiet text. Serif or a slender sans. Everything left-aligned to grid lines.
direction.colour: A pale neutral ground with one deep ink taken from the photographs. No accent beyond a quiet link colour.
direction.imagery: Six to nine photographs from one set, in a deliberate mix of ratios (3:4, 4:5, 1:1, 16:10, 21:9). Square corners. Captions, if any, are one short line under an image in the soft ink.
direction.richness: Placement. The differing sizes and offsets create movement on a still page.
direction.pitfalls: Uneven is not random: every image edge lands on a column line, and offsets come from a small set of values. On a phone, keep the unevenness with alternating widths (100%, 72% left, 60% right) rather than stacking everything full width.

hero.name: Stepped title, two photographs
hero.blueprint: A pale neutral ground with 6vw side margins on a 12-column grid. Navigation is three small items on the top edge at 15px: one link hard left, the wordmark centred, the single action hard right. The headline is two words or short phrases on two lines in a thin serif at clamp(72px, 8.3vw, 128px), leading 1.0, stepping diagonally across the middle third of the screen: the first line starts at column 2 with its baseline at 44% of the height; the second is indented to start at column 6 and ends near column 12. Two photographs are placed against the step, both with square corners. A small 16:10 landscape in columns 10-12 hangs from 10% of the height and stops about 20px above the first line. A 4:5 photograph in columns 2-5 starts 24px under the first line's baseline, to the left of the indented second line, and is cropped by the bottom edge of the viewport. Under the second line, starting on column 6, one sentence at 20px in the soft ink, max 36ch. Columns 6-12 of the lower third stay empty.
hero.mobile: The step survives: the first line at 15vw flush to the 20px left margin, the second line indented by 22vw. The small landscape sits above the title at 46% of the width, pushed to the right margin. The tall photograph follows the title at 72% of the width on the left margin, cropped by the bottom of the screen; the sentence at 16px moves beneath it.
hero.headline: Two words or short phrases, one per line, at most 9 characters each so the indented second line fits a phone.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Frame run, one lifted
sections.blueprint: Columns 1–3 are a nearly empty column: the heading (two to four words at 24–28px) at the top, a link under it, and one or two short notes at 15px much further down, each level with the frame it describes. Columns 4–12 hold a run of six to eight frames of the same subject at one fixed height of 30vh, with natural widths and 6px gaps: the whole view, a tight crop of the same thing, a detail, the reverse side. The run is allowed to leave the right edge. One frame is lifted out of the row: shown at 2.2 times the row height with its bottom aligned to the row's bottom (flex row, align-items: end), so it stands above the others. Under each frame, at 15px: a name on the left and a single fact on the right. Square corners, no captions on the images.
sections.mobile: The heading and link sit on top. The lifted frame comes first at full width. The rest of the run scrolls sideways beneath it at a fixed height of 34vw with 4px gaps and scroll-snap, bleeding off the right edge. Notes are listed under the run at 15px.

sections.name: Drag row of moments
sections.blueprint: A story told left to right. Top row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin; at the right margin two solid square buttons, 48px each, for back and forward. Directly beneath, a solid bar 6px tall spans the full width in a soft tone, with a full-ink segment showing how far the row has been scrolled. Then the row itself: six to nine columns, each 280px wide with 32px gaps, in a horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap that bleeds off both viewport edges. Every column reads top to bottom: a one-line caption at 18px bold that carries the order in words ('We met', 'Two winters on', 'The move'), three lines at 15px in the soft ink, then 80–140px of empty space that varies per column, then a 4:5 portrait photograph. Because the spaces vary, the photographs' top edges rise and fall along the row.
sections.mobile: Columns are 72vw wide with 16px gaps, so the next one always shows at the right edge. The buttons are dropped; the 6px progress bar stays under the heading. The empty space inside columns shrinks to 32–64px but still varies from column to column.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

references.name: Tengile Malamala Collection
references.idea: Let the land and animals carry everything: one staggered hairline-serif headline over aerial footage, then cream pages of olive-green serif text with photographs placed at uneven sizes.
references.hero: Aerial river footage fills the viewport, slightly darkened. Three small white caps items sit on the top edge: an enquiry link hard left, a stacked three-line wordmark centred, 'menu' hard right. The headline is two words on two lines in thin serif capitals about 8.3vw tall: the first line starts 10% from the left, the second is indented to 40% and ends near 90%, so the pair steps diagonally across the middle third. Below, starting at the 50% line, a three-line serif sentence at about 20px and a small white square-cornered button with a separate arrow square beside it. The lower third is left to the water.
references.type: PP Fragment at hairline weight (220): capitals for the 120px headline, sentence case for 28-36px olive statements. Inter at 11-16px for labels, nav and small paragraphs. Three serif sizes, two sans sizes; the serif never goes bold.
references.colour: #f5eee9 #5c6e21 #181608 #e3e1d4 #ffffff — Warm cream page with every word, large or small, in one olive green; the footer inverts to a solid olive field with cream text. Photography supplies all other colour.
references.imagery: Wildlife and lodge photography, natural and saturated, square corners, no overlays. Mixed aspect ratios placed at different widths and vertical offsets; lodge listings use equal landscape triplets; hero and closing band are full-bleed aerials.
references.layout: Narrow 16px outer margins and a twelve-column grid used asymmetrically: label and small paragraph in the left columns, the large statement starting at the midpoint. Sections alternate between loosely scattered image pairs and tidy three-up rows.

sections.description: Cream field. A tiny sans caps label top-left. A 28px olive serif paragraph of eight lines occupies only the right half, starting at the midpoint. Far below on the left, a five-line 12px sans paragraph about 180px wide. Images are placed loose: a landscape elephant photo under the right text, a tall leopard portrait lower at the left margin, a wide crop of elephant legs upper right of the next screen. No two share a top edge or width.

A tiny caps label, then an olive serif statement at about 36px running the full width for four lines. Beneath: a sub-label, a 12px paragraph held to a third of the width, then three equal landscape photos with 8px gutters spanning margin to margin, each captioned below in small serif. The same block repeats for a second category; one tile is dimmed with a short caps line laid over it to mark it as not yet open.

A full-bleed aerial of an elephant crossing a sandbank with a short serif statement, a small sans paragraph and the white button-plus-arrow pair set in the right half only. It butts directly against a solid olive footer: five columns of small cream links under tiny caps headings in the top third, a large empty green area beneath, and a legal line along the bottom edge.

steal: Stagger a two-line headline: first line from the left margin, second indented by 30% so the pair steps diagonally across the image.
Set every piece of text in a single brand colour on cream and make the footer that same colour as a solid field.
Split the button into two adjacent squares, label and arrow, with a 4px gap, small and square-cornered, instead of one pill.
references.media: A 10s muted aerial montage covers the whole first screen with type set on it and no visible scrim. Below: a split with an image and paragraph in the right half from the centre line, staggered image pairs with uneven heights and offsets, a three-up card row with captions, an inset full-width slider, a constellation of thumbnails round a centred heading, a slow portrait marquee, and a sticky full-bleed landscape with the closing call scrolling over it; 33 images, pictures oversized about 110% in their masks for drift.
references.motion: There is no preloader and only the montage cuts after 400ms, but under Lenis content stays hidden until each reveal fires: blocks rise and sharpen from a blur over 1.6s cubic-bezier(0.19,1,0.22,1), others fade with a filter over 1s cubic-bezier(0.165,0.84,0.44,1), pictures drift inside their masks, and the closing landscape holds on a sticky root. The ground steps from cream to sage-beige to olive, and the marquee loops on 120s.

references.name: Kononenko Architectural Bureau
references.idea: Let the renders do the talking: one full-bleed visualisation, a name set half in grotesk and half in serif, then alternating oversized sans and serif statements on white.
references.hero: A single architectural render fills the viewport edge to edge: a low grey metal-clad building under a large overcast sky, wild grass across the bottom third. Type is white and tiny except for the name. Top-left at a 24px margin, the bureau name is stacked on three lines at 13px. Top-right, four links run inline separated by commas, the current one underlined. Bottom-left, the name repeats at 60px (4.2vw) on two tight lines, the first two words in grotesk and the last word in a serif at the same size. No button, no scrim, no tagline; the sky takes the upper 45% untouched.
references.type: Two faces (digest names are obfuscated): a tight neo-grotesk at −0.03em and a soft high-contrast serif, mixed inside one line in the name. Section statements alternate: centred sans at about 6.5vw, then left-aligned serif at 4.5vw with a first-line indent. Labels are 9px.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #b7b7b9 #7c8050 #3d3a36 #9a9a9a — White pages with black type; colour comes only from the renders' overcast greys, greens and dark timber. The footer inverts to solid black with white letters.
references.imagery: Photoreal architectural visualisations in muted natural light, shown full-bleed at wide panoramic crops with square corners and no overlays; one loose black ink sketch on white stands in for process.
references.layout: 24px outer margins. Full-bleed image bands alternate with white type-only screens. Big statements either centre or run the full width; small data sits in narrow columns with tiny serif labels left of sans values, and hairline tables are inset to the right-hand third.

sections.description: White screen with a two-line sans heading centred at roughly 6.5vw, tight leading, taking the top third. Directly beneath, two tiny grey captions of two lines each sit side by side, each about 130px wide, centred as a pair. A full-bleed panoramic render starts immediately below and runs off the bottom, so the heading reads as a caption to the picture.

Far left, three label and value pairs at 9px (serif label, sans value) stack in a 150px column. From 34% across, a five-line serif paragraph at about 22px runs to 90% of the width. 120px lower a second row repeats the logic for achievements: a label at far left, then two narrow list columns of awards and publications at 9px with generous gaps between them.

A four-line serif statement at 4.5vw spans the full width, left-aligned with the first line indented about 3% and leading under 1. Below it, pushed into the right-hand 35% of the page, an offices table: a tiny label hangs to its left, and each row holds office type, country and city in grey, an address, and a small arrow, divided by hairlines at 18px row height.

Solid black. A top band of five tiny columns (name, navigation, media, address, hours), each a grey label beside a white list. Then a four-letter abbreviation of the name in white grotesk fills the entire width, letters about 45% of the viewport tall and touching both edges, with a single 8px legal line squeezed beneath.

steal: Set the last word of a sans headline in an upright serif of the same size to give a plain name a signature without any graphic device.
Alternate statement voices down the page: a centred grotesk heading, then a full-width left-aligned serif paragraph at display size with a first-line indent.
Close with an abbreviation of the name scaled until it touches both edges of a black footer, with all practical links shrunk to 9px above it.
references.media: One photoreal render covers the whole first screen with only the title docked bottom-left and no scrim. Below: a full-bleed 2:1 band under a centred headline, overscanned 32px per side for parallax, a staggered two-column scatter of landscape and portrait frames at uneven offsets, hand sketches drawn into the white page between statements, and a ring of small rotated square team photographs round a centred headline on black; 27 images and a fixed WebGL layer, no video.
references.motion: A white preloader with a progress line along the top and a counter stalled near 60 for 2.5s; by 4.5s the hero is in and the title rises out of a mask line by line. Lenis over the fixed WebGL layer: sketches build stroke by stroke on a scrub, the ground flips white to black over 0.3s at the values chapter, paragraph lines rise over 0.5s, and team photographs spiral in and settle into a ring; one ease for everything, cubic-bezier(.17,.84,.44,1), 34 uses.

references.name: longbow
references.idea: The page is built on a visible four-column construction grid with square handles at every intersection, and cars, glass cards and a giant condensed marquee are slotted into its cells like objects on a designer's artboard.
references.hero: Mid-grey studio video of two roadsters fills the viewport inside a thin outer frame. White hairlines split it into four equal columns and two rows, with small white square nodes at each crossing. A frosted-glass nav bar sits top centre spanning the two middle columns: hamburger left, condensed wordmark centre, a mono models link right. Bottom left, a white condensed marquee of the brand name at 21vw, a third of viewport height, runs off the left edge and stops at the centre line. The bottom-right cell holds a small glass tag, a two-line serif headline with the second line italic, and a six-line uppercase mono paragraph.
references.type: Bebas Neue at 21vw with -0.06em tracking for marquee words; EB Garamond near 28px, light, with italic second lines for headings; Geist Mono 13px uppercase for all body and labels. Three faces with strict roles and a roughly 23-times jump from body to display.
references.colour: #888c8f #a8a7a9 #ffffff #1b1b1c #1f5c49 #b5552e — One mid grey for both page and studio backdrop with white type throughout; colour comes only from the product: racing-green paint, tan leather, red tail lamps. One black video band late in the page.
references.imagery: Studio renders and video of cars on a seamless grey backdrop that matches the page colour, cropped tight to noses, tails and badges; images are square-cornered and sized exactly to grid cells or run full bleed.
references.layout: Four equal columns with visible hairlines and node markers persist down the whole 18-screen page. Content occupies one or two cells at a time and leaves the others as flat grey; giant marquee words and full-bleed car frames alternate with small serif-plus-mono text cells.

sections.description: A full-bleed close-up of one car fills the viewport. A dark frosted-glass card exactly one column wide and about half the viewport tall sits over the image in the second column: centred serif model name with an italic edition line, a mono price line, a small landscape thumbnail of the car and a white square-cornered button. The next model repeats the layout with the card shifted to the third column.

Flat grey screen. A giant white condensed marquee line runs across the top, partly behind the nav. In the first column: a tiny rounded index tag, a two-line serif heading with italic second line, then after a gap a ten-line uppercase mono paragraph. In the third column a tall portrait crop of bodywork and badge fills one cell from the marquee down. The other two columns stay empty.

Between sections, three condensed white words about a third of the viewport high are distributed across the grid columns with wide gaps between them and cropped by the viewport bottom, acting as a divider between a full-bleed car frame and the next text block. Grid lines and nodes run over the letters.

A black band holds a wide video frame inset from left and right by black bars, showing a motion-blurred car head-on on a road in a cool teal grade; the grid lines and nodes continue over it and the grey page resumes below. A single-line uppercase mono legal ticker runs along the very bottom edge of the page.

steal: Draw the layout grid as visible hairlines with small square nodes at intersections and size every image and card to exact cells.
Match the page background to the photo backdrop colour so product shots merge with the page and only the product carries colour.
Give three faces fixed jobs: a condensed sans only at 20vw for marquees, a light serif with an italic second line for headings, uppercase mono for all body text.
references.media: A full-bleed studio film of two cars covers the whole first screen with a slow push-in, shot on a grey cyclorama tuned to the page grey so pictures melt into the ground. Then a single-cell product card with a looping thumbnail over a full-bleed render, a checkerboard of image and text cells snapped to a 4-column grid, a driving film that grows from a 710px inset to full bleed, and portrait cells beside signature cells; 38 images and 14 videos, all square-cornered.
references.motion: No preloader: the page is alive at 400ms with the wordmark marquee moving and the hero film dollying in about 10% by 4.5s. Lenis with Webflow Interactions scrubs a sticky stage for the whole page: giant split words and their copies slide sideways at different rates, the inset film grows to full bleed, the ground switches grey, black, grey, black, and images reveal by mask-size and opacity over 1.25s ease-in-out while marquees loop at 9-90s.
